books.title_zh: 给一个青年诗人的十封信
books.author: rainer-maria-rilke
books.theme_zh: 没有任何人能给你建议，只有向内走这一条路
books.theme_en: Nobody can advise you; there is only one way, and it leads inward

prose.description_zh: 这是里尔克 1903 至 1908 年间写给一位素不相识的维也纳青年军官卡普斯的十封回信。卡普斯在军校读到里尔克的诗，写信请求评判自己的习作，并征询该走文学道路还是继续军官生涯。里尔克没有逐首点评，只反复回答同一个问题：不要向外界索取答案，回去向内挖。第一封信讲艺术家不该依赖批评；第二封信谈讽刺与那些无可替代的读物；第三封信提出忍耐就是一切；第四封信讨论爱与性的创造力；第五、六封信在罗马写独处与观看的方式；第七封信警告不给自己留独处空间的人容易滑向失败；第八封信写悲伤终将过去；第九封信谈情感与纪律；第十封信把艺术当作一种生活方式，并质疑半艺术的生涯。1929 年由卡普斯整理出版后，这十封信成为二十世纪被引用最多的创作与人生箴言之一。全书讨论的不是如何写诗，而是一个人如何面对孤独、比较、职业选择与无解的处境。
prose.description_en: These are Rainer Maria Rilke's replies to Franz Xaver Kappus, a junior officer at a military academy in Vienna who wrote to him in 1902 asking him to judge his poems and to advise him on whether to pursue literature or a military career. Rilke declined to critique the poems line by line and instead kept returning to one answer: do not look outward for permission, go into yourself. The ten letters, written between 1903 and 1908, move from the artist's independence from criticism, to irony and the irreducibly necessary books, to the injunction that patience is everything, to love and sexual creativity, to solitude and the way of seeing worked out in Rome, to the warning that those who make no room for solitude drift toward failure, to grief as a tension that passes, to emotion and discipline, and finally to art as a way of life rather than a half-profession. Kappus assembled and published them in 1929. What the book is really about is not poetry technique but how a person confronts solitude, comparison, professional doubt and situations without a clean solution.
prose.why_read_zh: 它的价值不在励志，而在把「向内」这个动作说清楚了。里尔克指出，提问本身就说明你还没有答案；去看评论、找导师、问别人行不行，都只是把决定权交出去，等于放弃了形成判断这件事。他给出的替代方案不是苦行，而是把等待变成工作：第十封信提出把艺术当作生活方式而非半吊子职业，第一封信要求创作者从自身的必要性里长出作品，而不是从市场的需要里领受任务。这套论证可以直接迁移到任何需要长期投入而短期看不到反馈的事上——写作、科研、做产品、学一门手艺。值得注意的是它并不正确：批评者指出里尔克的美学姿态回避了具体的社会与经济条件，把「忍耐」讲得过于高尚。但正是这种可被反驳的地方，让它仍然值得读。经典性证据（命中 4 项）：① 英文维基百科有独立书籍条目 Letters to a Young Poet，详载德文原名 Briefe an einen jungen Dichter、十封信写于 1903—1908 年、收信人为维也纳青年军官 Franz Xaver Kappus、1929 年由卡普斯整理、Insel Verlag 在莱比锡出版，并逐封说明十封信的时间地点与主题，非仅在作者条目中被提及；② Goodreads 评分 4.26、逾 13 万人评分（134,780 ratings / 17,160 reviews，多版本条目一致），达到「≥4.0 且评分人数 ≥5000」门槛；③ 权威书评媒体与机构评价：茨威格、冯至、北岛、茨威塔耶娃等在中文读者中口碑极高，德文维基条目记其为理解里尔克诗歌观念与工作过程的关键文献；④ 豆瓣读书中文版《给一个青年诗人的十封信》评分 9.0、6,975 人评价（冯至译，商务印书馆 2020 全新版另有 14,752 人 9 分好评），达到「豆瓣评分 ≥8.5 且评价人数 ≥1000」门槛。未计入项：英文维基页面未提及冯至中译，故译者信息以中文正式出版信息（商务印书馆）与冯至译本为准；微信读书推荐值本次未取得可核验数值，不计入、不编造；Goodreads 另见 Mary D. Herter Norton 英译本条目评分同为 4.26、133,989 人评分，已达门槛但不重复计数。时间检验：1929 年首版，至 2026-11-20 已满 97 年，远超 ≥5 年门槛。
prose.why_read_en: Its value is not motivational but clarifying: Rilke makes the inward motion precise. He notes that the fact of asking means you do not yet have an answer, and that seeking permission from critics, teachers or the market is a way of handing over the decision and giving up the formation of judgement. The alternative he offers is not austerity but the conversion of waiting into work — the tenth letter treats art as a way of life rather than a half-profession, and the first demands that the maker grow a work out of his own necessity rather than out of what is being asked of him. That argument transfers directly to any long investment without short-term feedback: writing, research, product work, learning a craft. It is not beyond dispute, either. Critics note that the aesthetic stance evades concrete social and economic conditions and elevates patience into something almost too noble. That refutability is precisely what keeps the book worth reading.
core_ideas_zh: 没有人能给你建议，只有向内走这一条路：外部评价只能制造依赖，不能产生作品
忍耐是创作的前置条件：艺术与理解都需要向内挖的漫长过程，而非立刻求得的答案
提问本身证明你还没有答案：把决定权交出去的那一刻，判断力就停止生长
艺术应当是一种生活方式，而不是一种半职业；只有把全部生活当作材料的人，才写得出真正属于自己的东西
core_ideas_en: Nobody can advise you; there is only one way, and it leads inward — external judgement produces only dependence, never work
Patience is a precondition of making: art and understanding both require a long inward excavation rather than a quickly available answer
The very act of asking proves you have no answer yet; the moment you hand the decision away, judgement stops developing
Art should be a way of life rather than a half-profession; only those who treat all of life as material write anything truly their own
key_questions_zh: 当所有人都在告诉你该怎么走时，凭什么判断一条建议是为你而设的，还是把他自己的恐惧包装成忠告？
在没有反馈、没有听众、甚至没有成果的阶段里，人靠什么继续把事情做下去？
key_questions_en: When everyone tells you how to live, how do you tell an answer made for you from his fear dressed up as advice?
In stages with no feedback, no audience and no visible result, what keeps a person working?
prose.who_should_read_zh: 适合正在做一件长期、孤独、回报延迟的事的人：写作者、研究者、独立开发者、准备离开稳定轨道去尝试另一种生活的人。也适合读过很多「如何写作」「如何成功」却仍不确定自己为什么写的人，以及正在被比较、评价与职业路径困扰的年轻人。语言是散文体的书信，不艰涩，一次读十封信的时间成本很低，但需要在安静时读。
prose.who_should_read_en: For anyone doing something long, solitary and slow to pay off: writers, researchers, independent developers, and people about to leave a stable track to try another life. It also suits readers who have worked through many books on how to write or how to succeed and still cannot say why they write, and young people weighed down by comparison, evaluation and career paths. The prose is plain, letter-form, and cheap to read in a single sitting — but it asks for quiet.
prose.reading_note_zh: 先读第一封信与第十封信，它们是全书的两端：第一封讲不要向外求，第三封讲忍耐就是一切，第十封讲把艺术过成一种生活方式。中段六封信可以按主题跳读——第四、五、六封谈爱、观看与独处，第八封写悲伤，最容易被单独抽出的一封。建议一次只读一封信，中间留出几天，否则容易把忍耐读成一种安慰而不是一份工作。最合适的搭配是同代人的对照文本，比如蒙田随笔或里尔克自己的《马尔特·布里格随笔》，看同一种「向内」在两个气质迥异的人那里如何落地。
prose.reading_note_en: Start with the first and tenth letters, which are the two ends of the book: the first on not looking outward for permission, the third on patience being everything, the tenth on living art as a way of life. The middle letters reward being read by theme — the fourth, fifth and sixth on love, seeing and solitude, the eighth on grief — and any one of them can be lifted out on its own. Read one letter at a time and leave days between them, or patience will turn into consolation rather than a job description. A good companion is a text of the same period in a different temperament, such as Montaigne's Essays or Rilke's own The Notebooks of Malte Laurids Brigge, to see how two very different people work out the same inwardness.

books.title_zh: 为什么学生不喜欢上学？
books.author: daniel-willingham
books.theme_zh: 大脑不是用来思考的：学习是一套可被设计的工程
books.theme_en: The mind is not built for thinking; learning is an engineering problem that can be designed

prose.description_zh: 认知心理学家丹尼尔·威林厄姆用九年实验与上千名学生的数据回答一个看似简单的问题：为什么学生不喜欢学校？他的答案分两步。第一步是反直觉的：学生不是天生讨厌学习，而是大脑本就不是为思考而设计的——它更擅长避免思考、识别模式、走熟路。所以走神不是意志薄弱，而是节能；学生能记住偶像剧剧情却记不住历史考点，是因为熟练加工几乎不耗能，而抽象推理极其耗能。第二步他给出九条原则：工作记忆容量只有几项，是所有思考的硬瓶颈；事实性知识是思维技能的前提，没有背景知识就谈不上批判性思维；记忆是思考的残留物，因此理解必须有意义；反复练习是走向精通的唯一道路；智力是可变的而非固定的；所谓学习风格并不存在，个体差异远小于教学方式的差异。全书用认知科学为教师和家长提供了一套可操作的判断标准，而不是一堆教育口号。
prose.description_en: Cognitive scientist Daniel Willingham answers a deceptively simple question — why don't students like school? — with two moves. The first is counterintuitive: students do not hate learning by nature, but the brain is not built for thinking. It is built to avoid thinking, to detect patterns and to run familiar routines. Inattention is therefore energy-saving rather than a failure of will; students remember television plots but not history lessons because fluent processing is nearly free while abstract reasoning is expensive. The second move is a set of nine principles. Working memory holds only a handful of items and is a hard bottleneck on thinking. Factual knowledge comes before thinking skills: without background knowledge there is no critical thinking to speak of. Memory is the residue of thought, so understanding must be meaningful. Repeated practice is the only road to mastery. Intelligence is malleable rather than fixed. And so-called learning styles do not exist: differences between children are far smaller than differences between teaching methods. The book turns laboratory cognitive science into judgements a teacher or parent can actually use, rather than a further set of slogans about education.
prose.why_read_zh: 这本书的价值在于把「学不会」从一个道德问题改写成工程问题。孩子不愿意背历史、不愿意做题，往常被解释成态度问题、动机问题或者老师的问题；威林厄姆的框架把它还原为认知资源与教学设计问题：工作记忆就那么几格，一节课塞十个概念必然失败；把知识讲得有趣却不让它进入工作记忆，孩子照样什么都学不到。这个转换可迁移到你自己的任何学习计划上——它告诉你为什么间隔重复、先建事实框架再谈应用、讲给别人听这些做法有效，而不是只告诉你这么做有效。更重要的是它敢于自我设限：作者反复强调，把实验室里的认知科学直接搬进课堂，效果证据并不一致，九条原则是给专业判断用的起点，不是免检通行证。这份克制让它比同类畅销书可靠得多。经典性证据（命中 3 项）：① Goodreads 评分 4.04、逾 6000 人评分（6,011 ratings / 650 reviews，多版本条目一致），达到「≥4.0 且评分人数 ≥5000」门槛；② 豆瓣读书中文版《为什么学生不喜欢上学？》评分 9.2、逾 3000 人评价（江苏教育出版社 2010-05 版，赵萌译、朱永新审校，另有 9.3 分 2,289 人评分记录），达到「豆瓣评分 ≥8.5 且评价人数 ≥1000」门槛；③ 权威书评媒体长评：《The Wall Street Journal》刊出书评并称威林厄姆的结论同样适用于课堂之外的企业培训者、营销人员与家长（"Mr. Willingham's answers apply just as well outside the classroom"）。未计入项：英文维基百科原「Why Don't Students Like School?」独立条目已于 2026-11-18 被删除（删除理由为疑似 LLM 生成内容），故本次不计入维基独立条目一项，该条证据已弃用、不引用；微信读书推荐值与 Google Scholar 引用数本次未取得可核验数值，不计入、不编造；中国青年出版社 2023 年第 2 版豆瓣 8.3、578 人评价未达门槛，不计入。时间检验：2009 年首版，至 2026-11-20 已满 17 年，超过 ≥5 年门槛。
prose.why_read_en: The book is valuable because it recasts a failure to learn from a moral question into an engineering one. A child who will not drill dates or grind through problems is usually blamed for attitude, motivation or a bad teacher; Willingham's framework puts it back where it belongs, in cognitive resource limits and instructional design. Working memory holds only a few items, so a lesson that packs ten new concepts must fail, and a fun explanation that never lands inside working memory leaves the learner with nothing. That reframing transfers to any study plan of your own: it explains why spaced repetition, building factual scaffolding before application, and teaching the material to someone else work, rather than merely instructing you to do them. Just as important, the book limits itself. Willingham repeatedly notes that moving laboratory cognitive science straight into classrooms has produced inconsistent evidence, and that the nine principles are a starting point for professional judgement, not a certificate of exemption. That restraint makes it far more reliable than the usual bestsellers in this genre.
core_ideas_zh: 大脑不是为思考而设计的：默认状态是避免思考，走神是节能而非意志薄弱
工作记忆是硬约束：思考的瓶颈是同时可处理的项数，不是智力高低，容量小就无法靠努力绕过
事实先于思维技能：没有背景知识，所谓批判性思维只是空中楼阁，必须先建立知识框架
记忆是思考的残留物：只有理解了意义的东西才留得下来，因此教学要制造意义而非只求覆盖
智力是可变的：能力差距更多来自知识与练习的累积，而非天赋的固定分配
core_ideas_en: The mind is not designed for thinking: avoiding thought is the default, so inattention is energy-saving rather than weakness of will
Working memory is a hard constraint: the bottleneck on thinking is how many items can be handled at once, not how intelligent one is
Facts come before thinking skills: without background knowledge there is no critical thinking to speak of, so scaffolding must come first
Memory is the residue of thought: only what has been understood meaningfully survives, so teaching must create meaning rather than merely cover material
Intelligence is malleable: gaps in achievement come more from accumulated knowledge and practice than from a fixed distribution of talent
key_questions_zh: 当一个人反复学不会同一件事时，问题究竟出在动机、天赋，还是知识结构与教学设计本身？
把认知科学的结论搬到真实课堂里，哪些能稳定复现，哪些只在实验室里成立？
key_questions_en: When someone repeatedly fails to learn the same thing, is the problem motivation, talent, or the structure of the knowledge and the design of the teaching?
When cognitive science is moved out of the laboratory into real classrooms, which findings replicate reliably and which do not?
prose.who_should_read_zh: 写给所有要教别人或者自学的人：教师、家长、教练、带团队的技术负责人，也包括正在准备考试或转行的人。它最有用的读者是那些已经在实践中试过各种方法却说不清为什么有效的人——这本书会给他们的直觉提供机制层面的解释。需要一点耐心：作者会先讲工作记忆和练习效应这些反直觉的结论，需要一点耐心读到最后才能把九条原则串成一套完整判断。中文版由江苏教育出版社出版，译本可读性好。
prose.who_should_read_en: Written for everyone who teaches or teaches themselves: teachers, parents, coaches, engineering managers leading teams, and people studying for exams or changing careers. Its most useful reader is someone who has already tried many methods in practice and cannot say why any of them worked — this book supplies the mechanism behind the intuition. It asks for some patience: Willingham starts with counterintuitive findings about working memory and the effect of practice, and only near the end do the nine principles cohere into a single judgement. The Chinese edition reads well.
prose.reading_note_zh: 按顺序读，不必跳，但每读完一章先停下来想一个具体的人：你的学生、你的孩子，或者你自己。第九条原则关于学习风格的讨论最容易被忽视，也最该先看——它是全书里最少被引用、却最能立刻改变教学行为的一条。读完可以对照《认知天性》与 Dunlosky 等人 2013 年对学习策略有效性的元分析，看看哪些结论被后续研究支持、哪些仍在争议。全书只有九章，一个晚上可以读完第一部分，但真正的价值在读完后拿它去改一份具体的教学或学习方案。
prose.reading_note_en: Read it in order, without skipping, but after each chapter stop and think of one concrete person: your students, your child, or yourself. The discussion of learning styles is the least cited of the nine principles and the one most likely to change your behaviour immediately. Afterwards, compare it with Make It Stick and with Dunlosky and colleagues' 2013 meta-analysis of learning techniques, to see which conclusions have been supported by later research and which remain contested. The book is only nine chapters long; the first part takes an evening, but the real value comes from taking it to rewrite one concrete teaching or study plan.
